document_title: Cameras ride 50 Dallas brush trucks. Staff review what they flag
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Cameras ride 50 Dallas brush trucks.

The trucks keep the routes they already run. The software is City Detect. It flags possible exterior property and right-of-way conditions along the way.

The city's October 19th briefing says an observation is not a confirmed Code violation. It says trained staff review every one before Code Compliance acts. In a prioritized inspection a Code Inspector goes on site to find out whether a violation exists.

The first letter a resident got used to be a formal notice of violation. The briefing says a first courtesy letter is now an educational reminder with no deadline.

The October 19th briefing publishes no accuracy figure. It lists calibrating detection accuracy and setting accuracy measures as next steps. How accurate was the camera across the 5,318 observations reviewed?

#Dallas #CityDetect #CodeCompliance

S1.headline: Cameras ride 50 brush trucks
S1.body: The trucks already run routine Sanitation routes, the city's October 19th briefing says. An April city memo planned two cameras per truck. The truck is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: 50 trucks, 100 cameras planned
S2.body: The December 2025 plan priced the system at $852,000 a year for 100 cameras, with a human in the loop for all actions. The yard is drawn to illustrate.

S3.headline: The camera flags. Staff decide, the city says.
S3.body: City Detect flags possible conditions along the route for trained staff to review. The city says an observation is not a confirmed Code violation, and faces and license plates are blurred. Drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: 5,318 observations, each one reviewed

S5.headline: What the city counted

S6.headline: A courtesy letter sets no deadline
S6.body: The table counts 2,928 courtesy notices. A courtesy letter is now an educational reminder outside the citation process, the briefing says. The first letter used to be a formal notice of violation. Drawn to illustrate.

S8.headline: Accuracy is still a next step

S9.headline: People make the decisions, the city says
S9.body: The October 19th briefing to the Quality of Life, Arts, and Culture Committee says success is not measured by citations. The December 2025 plan proposed $852,000 a year on a contract the city could end with 10 days written notice. Drawn to illustrate.
